provenance.l: Apollo 17 Mission Report (Tables 3-I and 3-V, sections 3.2 to 3.4): range zero 05:33:00 GMT 1972-12-07. A direct rendezvous with two CSM burns before the LM left the Moon: orbital trim 178:54:05 (RCS, 37 s, 9.2 ft/s) to 67.3 x 62.5 n.mi because "the planned decay of the CSM altitude ... was not realized. This was similar to the experience of Apollo 15", plane change 179:53:54 (20.05 s from SP-4029, RCS; the MR OCR reads 23.1 s service propulsion: a disagreement; no delta-V read), then the LM vernier 10 ft/s at 185:32:12 (no duration read: 8 s is an estimate), TPI 186:15:58 (3.1 s, about 54 ft/s) and TPF (no GET, duration or delta-V in the sources read: 186:58:00, 42 min after TPI as on Apollos 14-16, and 25 s are estimates). Ascent 441 s and 6,075.7 ft/s (OCR), orbit 48.5 x 9.1 n.mi (OCR), insertion 185:28:56 (SP-4029 prints the burn to 185:28:58); docking 187:37:15; ascent stage jettison 191:18:31, deorbit 192:58:14, impact 193:17:20.8 at 19 deg 57 min 58 s N, 30 deg 29 min 23 s E (not shown); TEI 234:02:09.18, 143.69 s, 3,046.3 ft/s; no subsatellite on Apollo 17. All times are the mission report / SP-4029 clock; entry compilation figures are in the splashdown profile

NASA SP-4029 Apollo 17 timeline: GET and GMT of liftoff, docking, jettison, the SIM bay door and the subsatellite events. Apollo 17 SIM bay: door jettisoned 081:32:40 (MR17 Table 3-I); the bay carries the lunar sounder, infrared radiometer and UV spectrometer, not a subsatellite or spectrometer booms
NASA SP-4029 Apollo 17 trans-Earth phase: TEI burn duration, delta-V and flight-path angle at cutoff
